widget.name: Auto Drag and Drop
widget.description: Makes the rows of a list you already have draggable. Place it in a row, pick the sort attribute, and set On drop (Events tab) to Save changes.

property.caption: Show advanced settings
property.description: No: place the widget in a row of a Gallery, List view or Data grid 2, pick the sort attribute below, and set On drop (Events tab) to 'Save changes'. That is all. Yes: also drop zones (rows that move between lists), your own drop logic, and more settings for the row.

property.caption: Role
property.description: Handle: place it in a row (a gallery item, list view item or data grid row) to make that row draggable; it draws the six dots there. Drop zone: only needed when rows move between lists (lanes, groups) or into an empty list.

property.caption: Group
property.description: Only matters with drop zones: rows can only be dropped in drop zones with the same group name. Give nested lists (for example packages and the lines inside them) different names.

property.caption: Disabled
property.description: Optional. When true, this row cannot be dragged / this drop zone accepts no drops.

property.caption: Sort attribute
property.description: The attribute that holds the order of the rows, e.g. Sequence. Sort the list by it. The widget gives the rows that change place each other's numbers; the user needs write access to this attribute.

property.caption: Drag by
property.description: Whole row: the row can be picked up anywhere; buttons, links and inputs in it keep working. On touch a short press picks it up, so a swipe still scrolls. Six dots only: dragging starts on the dots only, so text in the row stays selectable.

property.caption: Show six dots
property.description: Draw the six-dot grip where this widget is placed, as a sign that the row can be dragged. On touch a press on the dots picks the row up at once. The dots are also what a keyboard user focuses.

property.caption: Sequencing
property.description: Automatic: the widget changes the sort attribute of the rows that change place, then runs On drop for each of them; set On drop to 'Save changes'. Manual: the widget changes nothing; On drop runs once, for the dragged row, and gets the new position (newSortValue, newIndex) to store the order yourself. Rows that move between drop zones are always manual.

property.caption: Item key
property.description: Optional. Unique key of this row (e.g. toString($currentObject/StatusID)). Passed to the drop actions: the dragged row's key to a drop zone's action, and the keys of the new neighbours to both.

property.caption: Row (CSS selector)
property.description: Optional. The element that moves: the closest element around this widget that matches this selector. Leave empty for the gallery item, list view item or data grid row this widget sits in.

property.caption: Handle label
property.description: Optional. Text for screen readers and the tooltip of the six dots. Leave empty for the built-in text in the user's language (Dutch, German or English).

property.caption: Zone key
property.description: Key of this drop zone (e.g. toString($currentObject/StatusID)), passed to the drop actions as the zone a row came from or went to.

property.caption: Drop zone is
property.description: What forms the drop zone. An element around this widget: place the widget anywhere inside the lane or group and name that element with a CSS selector. The content of this widget: place the list inside the widget; the widget draws a box around it and that box is the drop zone.

property.caption: Element (CSS selector)
property.description: The drop zone is the closest element around this widget that matches this selector, e.g. .board-lane. The widget must sit inside that element.

property.caption: Content
property.description: The list that forms the drop zone.

property.caption: On drop
property.description: With automatic sequencing: choose 'Save changes' (Close page: No). It runs for every row whose number changed, so the new order is stored. With manual sequencing: runs once for the dragged row, with the variables below.

actionVariable.caption: 0-based position among the rows shown in the target list, without the dragged row
Manual sequencing: sort value between the neighbours: average of both, row below - 1, row above + 1, or 0 in an empty list (needs Sort attribute on the rows)
Zone key of the drop zone the row was dropped in (empty without drop zones)
Zone key of the drop zone the row came from (empty without drop zones)
Item key of the row it was dropped after (empty = at the start)
Item key of the row it was dropped before (empty = at the end)

property.caption: On drop in zone
property.description: Drop zone only. Runs when a row is dropped in this zone, with this zone's object as context.

actionVariable.caption: Item key of the dragged row
Zone key the row was dragged from (empty when it was not in a zone)
Item key of the row it was dropped after (empty = at the start)
Item key of the row it was dropped before (empty = at the end)
0-based position in this zone among the rows shown, without the dragged row
Sort value between the neighbours: average of both, row below - 1, row above + 1, or 0 when the zone is empty (needs Sort attribute on the rows)

property.caption: Animate list changes
property.description: Slide the rows of this list to their new place whenever the list changes (a row is added, removed or moved), not only after a drag. The two settings below also set the speed of the drag itself, so they stay in use when this is off.

property.caption: Duration
property.description: How long a row takes to move to another place, in milliseconds: when it makes room during a drag, settles after a drop, or the list changes. A new row takes a little longer to come in. 0 = no animation.

property.caption: Animation flow
property.description: How rows speed up and slow down while they move.

enumerationValues.enumerationValue: Ease in-out (slow start and slow end)
Linear (same speed from start to end)
